44-036.r: Wrong pair: Cornwallis - Third Anglo-Maratha War → it was under Lord Hastings (1817-18). Correct: Hector Munro - Buxar; Lord Hastings - Anglo-Nepal War; Wellesley - Fourth Anglo-Mysore War.

44-038.r: Sir Thomas Munro → Governor of Madras 1820-1827; father of the Ryotwari System (land tax collected directly from the ryots).

44-039.r: Governor-General who took over Mysore's administration citing maladministration → Lord William Bentinck (took charge July 1828; also abolished Sati).

44-040.r: Third Anglo-Mysore War (1790-1792) → Lord Cornwallis, who led the army himself; Treaty of Srirangapatna (1792) took about half of Tipu's state.

44-041.r: Suppression of Thugs → Captain Sleeman, appointed by Lord William Bentinck; arrested 1562 thugs between 1826 and 1835. Thugs worshipped Kali, Durga or Bhavani.

44-043.r: Bentinck's social reforms → abolished Sati (1829), slavery abolished by the Charter Act 1833, campaign against Thugs; not 'removal of disabilities due to change of religion'.

44-044.r: Sati abolished → Lord William Bentinck, 1829. Sati means 'holy and virtuous woman'.

44-047.r: 'Hill Assembly Plan' for Pahariya tribals → Cleveland; hills under hereditary chiefs (sardars) in an assembly that met twice a year, with power over capital punishment.

44-048.r: Export of slaves from Bengal banned → 1789; slavery declared illegal across India 1843; made a crime under the Indian Penal Code 1860.

44-049.r: Awadh annexed (Feb 1856) by declaring it maladministered → Dalhousie accused Nawab Wajid Ali Shah; not by Doctrine of Lapse or war.
44-049.t: Awadh = maladministration; Satara, Jhansi, Nagpur = Doctrine of Lapse.

44-051.r: Not annexed under Doctrine of Lapse → Jaipur. Dalhousie's lapse list: Satara 1848, Jaitpur and Sambalpur 1849, Baghat 1850, Udaipur 1852, Jhansi 1853, Nagpur 1854.
44-051.h: Order S-J-S-B-U-J-N: "Some Jolly Sikhs Bring Up Juicy Nuts".

44-053.r: Not annexed by the British → Gwalior. Sind → under Ellenborough (1842-1844); Awadh → 1856 (maladministration, Dalhousie); Satara → 1848.

44-059.r: Order of annexation (Doctrine of Lapse, Dalhousie): Satara 1848 → Sambalpur (Orissa) 1849 → Jhansi 1854.

44-060.r: First victim of Dalhousie's Doctrine of Lapse → Satara (1848). Doctrine: a state lapsed to the British if its ruler died childless.

44-062.r: James Andrew Broun Ramsay → real name of Lord Dalhousie (Earl of Dalhousie), Governor-General from 1848.

44-063.r: Conquest of Sindh completed → under Lord Ellenborough (1842-1844); Charles Napier annexed it in 1843.

44-066.r: Lord Dalhousie annexed part of Sikkim, such as Darjeeling, on the excuse that the Sikkim king had mistreated two English doctors.

44-067.r: British Resident in Awadh at annexation → James Outram (replaced W.H. Sleeman, 1854); his report led to the merger in Feb 1856.
44-067.t: Henry Lawrence was Resident at Lucknow during the 1857 revolt, not at annexation.

44-068.r: First railway in India → Dalhousie's period, Bombay to Thane, 1853.

44-071.r: First railway service → Great Indian Peninsula Railway Company, 1853, Boribandar (Bombay) to Thane.

44-072.r: Last major extension of British India → Burma, added 1 January 1886 after the Third Anglo-Burma War (1885); Viceroy was Lord Dufferin.

44-073.r: Public Works Department → first set up in 1854 under Lord Dalhousie; public works were earlier under the army board.

44-074.r: Hindu Widow Remarriage Act 1856 (Act XV) → Lord Canning's period, through Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar's efforts; children of such marriages made legal.

44-075.r: Queen Victoria's Proclamation → read by Lord Canning (first Viceroy) at Allahabad, 1 Nov 1858; Government of India Act 1858 moved rule from Company to Crown.

44-078.r: Right of rulers to adopt an heir restored → Queen's Proclamation of 1858 (read at Allahabad, 1 Nov 1858); policy of annexation ended.

44-079.r: Queen Victoria made Empress of India → 1877.

44-080.r: Royal Titles Act passed 1876 → Queen Victoria proclaimed Empress of India on 1 January 1877 at Delhi.
44-080.t: Act 1876, proclamation 1877 - the question asks the proclamation year.

44-081.r: Slavery abolished by Act V of 1843 → Governor-General Lord Ellenborough (1842-1844).
44-081.t: Don't pick Bentinck; the abolishing Act came under Ellenborough.

44-082.r: Correct: Cornwallis → Permanent Settlement (1793). Masterly Inactivity → John Lawrence; Subsidiary Alliance → Wellesley; Doctrine of Lapse → Dalhousie; Congress founded (A.O. Hume) under Dufferin.

44-085.r: Wrong pair: Lord Hastings - Second Anglo-Maratha War → Second (1803-1805) was under Wellesley; Lord Hastings fought the Third (1817-18) and abolished the Peshwaship (1818).

44-087.r: Subordinate alliances with Rajputana states, 1817-18 → negotiated by Charles Metcalfe for Lord Hastings, against Marathas and Pindaris.

44-088.r: Wrong pair: Sir John Shore - Anglo-Nepal War → it was under Lord Hastings (1814-1815). Correct: Cornwallis - Permanent Settlement; Wellesley - Subsidiary Alliance; Hastings - Third Anglo-Maratha War.

44-089.r: Correct: Wellesley → Fourth Anglo-Mysore War (1799). Sindh → Ellenborough (March 1843); Awadh → Dalhousie (1856); Third Anglo-Maratha War → Lord Hastings (1817-18).

44-090.r: Wrong pair: Lytton - First Anglo-Afghan War → First (1839-1842) was under Auckland; Lytton had the Second (1878-80). Correct: Dalhousie - Awadh; Dufferin - Congress; Bentinck - Charter Act 1833.

44-091.r: Policy of 'Masterly Inactivity' towards Afghanistan → mainly John Lawrence (period from Ellenborough to Northbrook).

44-092.r: Financial Decentralisation in India → Lord Mayo, 1870.

44-093.r: First census in British India → 1872 under Lord Mayo (1869-72); regular census from 1881 under Lord Ripon.
44-093.t: Don't confuse first census (Mayo) with first regular census (Ripon).

44-095.r: Viceroy murdered by a convict in the Andaman and Nicobar Islands while on tour → Lord Mayo, the first Viceroy killed in office.

44-097.r: Mayo's Resolution 1870 → first split of Central and Provincial finances; provinces got services like education, medical, roads; aimed to fix imbalance and meet provincial needs. All correct.

44-099.r: Aggressive 'Forward Policy' towards Afghanistan → Lord Lytton (Viceroy 1876, appointed under Disraeli), replacing 'Masterly Inactivity'.

44-101.r: Lord Lytton (Viceroy 1876-1880) → Vernacular Press Act 1878, Indian Arms Act 1878, Strachey Commission; not the Ilbert Bill.
hi: Vernacular Press Act (देशी भाषा समाचार पत्र अधिनियम)

44-102.r: Longest tenure among the options → Lord Curzon (1899-1905); Hardinge 1910-1916; Dufferin 1884-1888; Mayo 1869-1872.

44-103.r: Local Self-Government strengthened by the resolution of 18 May 1882 → Lord Ripon, Viceroy under Gladstone's Liberal government (1880).

44-105.r: Ilbert Bill (1883, Viceroy Ripon) → let Indian judges and magistrates try British offenders in criminal cases at district level; fiercely opposed by Europeans.

44-106.r: First Factory Act 1881 → Lord Ripon: no children below 7 employed; children 7-12 max 9 hours a day; four holidays a month.

44-108.r: Father of Local Self-Government in India → Lord Ripon (resolution of 1882).
44-108.h: Ripon = Ripe local bodies: he "ripened" municipalities.

44-109.r: Wrong pair: Local self-government - Lytton → it was Ripon (1882). Correct: Subsidiary Alliance - Wellesley; Doctrine of Lapse - Dalhousie; Permanent Settlement - Cornwallis.

44-110.r: Clive → Dual Govt in Bengal (1765); Bentinck → English Education (Macaulay, 7 March 1835); Charles Metcalfe → removal of press restrictions; Curzon → Partition of Bengal.

44-111.r: Dalhousie → Doctrine of Lapse; William Bentinck → prohibition of Sati; Ripon → Local Self-Government; Curzon → division (Partition) of Bengal.

44-112.r: Correct: Ellenborough (1842-44) → annexation of Sindh, March 1843. Regulating Act made Warren Hastings first GG of Bengal; Permanent Settlement → Cornwallis, not Wellesley.

44-113.r: Dalhousie → Doctrine of Lapse; Curzon → Partition of Bengal; William Bentinck → prohibition of Sati; Cornwallis → Permanent Settlement of Bengal.

44-114.r: Archaeological Survey of India organised and centralised → Lord Curzon (John Marshall Director-General, 1901). Earlier: Asiatic Society 1784; Cunningham named Archaeological Surveyor 1861 by Canning.
hi: Archaeological Survey of India (भारतीय पुरातत्व सर्वेक्षण)

44-116.r: Department of Archaeological Survey set up in 1871 → under Governor General Mayo, on the advice of Secretary of State Duke of Argyll.
44-116.t: Curzon later reorganised and centralised the ASI; he did not first set it up.
44-116.c: Answer not printed; CGPSC cancelled the question since neither Mayo nor Argyll is an option.

44-117.r: Ancient Monuments Preservation Act, 1904 → passed under Lord Curzon.

44-118.r: G.K. Gokhale compared Lord Curzon's administration in India to that of Aurangzeb.

44-119.r: Imperial Cadet Corps (Nov 1901) → Lord Curzon; Commandant Major D.H. Cameron; honorary Commandant Maharaja Pratap Singh of Idar.

44-120.r: Viceroy order: Curzon (1899-1905) → Hardinge (1910-1916) → Chelmsford (1916-1921) → Irwin (1926-1931).

44-121.r: 1905: Curzon redrew provincial boundaries and split Bengal, creating the new province 'Eastern Bengal and Assam'. Both statements correct.

44-122.r: Curzon: "the message is carved in granite" (Empire built on rock) and Calcutta Municipal Act 1899, which cut elected Indian members. Both true.

44-123.r: 'Divide and Rule' → Lord Curzon and Lord Minto (both answers): Partition of Bengal 1905 as its symbol; Minto promoted separate electorates.
hi: Divide and Rule (फूट डालो और राज करो)

44-124.r: "Congress is tottering to its fall... assist it to a peaceful demise" → Lord Curzon (1900); he also mocked nationalist work as "letting off of gas".
